picked.angle: A Portuguese startup closes a 1.1 million euro round for a bedside lamp that uses an AI algorithm to detect night-time seizures.
read_at_source: tech.eu calls it 'The Portuguese startup'; round of 1.1 million euros led by Fundação Ageas and Portugal Ventures, with Angels Way, Phira Ventures and business angels

a smart bedside lamp with a small built-in camera and a proprietary AI algorithm that, the article says, detects movements that may indicate a seizure with over 97 per cent accuracy and alerts emergency contacts, with no wearable sensors
the funds are for a launch in Europe and the UK (per the search summary; the journalist re-reads the page)
care: The 97 per cent is the company's claim as reported: attribute it, do not state it as fact.
Name organisations only; do not name the individual angels listed.
Where the company is based is not stated in what I read beyond 'Portuguese'; do not say a city.
picked.licence: not checked: cite and link, do not copy

picked.angle: The Council of Ministers gives 'national strategic interest' status to Portugal's bid for an EU-co-funded AI gigafactory, which lets the site connect to the grid, up to 260 MVA, if Portugal wins the tender.
read_at_source: ECO: the Council of Ministers approved on Thursday (26 Nov) a Resolution giving the status of 'national strategic interest' to the Portuguese bid for one of the AI gigafactories co-funded by the European Commission
the Government's communiqué, as ECO quotes it: the Resolution ensures the conditions for connecting the project to the public electricity network with a capacity of up to 260 MVA
the grid connection applies if Portugal wins the tender
care: The primary source is the Government's communiqué on portugal.gov.pt; I quote it only through ECO and did not open it: the checker should read it before anything is published.
Say what the resolution does and that the tender is not yet won.
